Is the chicken you’re eating today really the same chicken people ate decades ago?  In this podcast, Khashif Khan reveals how industrial farming has transformed modern chicken production, raising questions about food quality, nutrition, inflammation, and long-term health.  According to Khan, chickens that once weighed around 1 kilogram are now being bred to reach up to 4 kilograms. He argues that modern poultry farming prioritizes faster growth, higher production, and lower costs over nutritional quality.  One of his biggest concerns is linoleic acid, an omega-6 fatty acid found in chicken meat. Khan suggests that changes in poultry feed and industrial farming practices may influence the fatty acid composition of chicken, potentially affecting inflammation and metabolic health.  However, omega-6 fatty acids are essential nutrients, and current scientific evidence does not establish that eating conventional chicken causes chronic inflammation. He also highlights the differences between factory-farmed chicken and organic, pasture-raised poultry, encouraging consumers to think more critically about food sourcing, farming practices, and the nutritional quality of their protein.  His broader message goes beyond chicken: modern food production often prioritizes affordability, shelf life, and consumer appeal, raising important questions about whole foods, processed foods, gut health, metabolic health, and longevity.  Are we optimizing our food system for human health or maximum production?
